title: Buddy Petit's tone, appearance and comparison with Sam Morgan
summary: Petit was small with a huge tone and played excursion boats; Sam Morgan had a better but rougher band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: What did Buddy Petit look like, by the way?

Well, Buddy, as I recall, was on the small side, but had a very, very powerful tone. And Buddy played on the excursion boats running from West End to Mandeville and Lewisburg. I don't know what arrangement he had with the boat people, but I would imagine that they played for practically the cost of the trip going over there, so they could play a date that night either in Mandeville or Covington or one of the surrounding towns. And the thing I remember most vividly about Buddy was with this powerful tone, and being as small as he was, he looked very funny because when he'd blow his neck would puff out to such a great extent. He looked like a cobra. And it was said that, I don't know how true, but that one Buddy blasted out, if he was in the middle of the lake you could hear him from either side. I doubt that statement, but nevertheless he was to have a very powerful...
How did he compare with Sam Morgan?

Actually, I don't think I've ever heard anyone blow any louder than Buddy. He had a tremendous volume to his horn. I've heard better cornet players, I guess, but none that could play any louder. I would say this too, that in Sam Morgan's case, I think Sam Morgan, from my memory, had a better band than Buddy. But he had a pretty rough band, as I recall it. Not smooth at all.
